sections.label: Pallavi
sections.ta:
எதுகையும் மோனையும் வேண்டுவதோ எம்பெருமான்
திருவருள் நினைந்து துதிபாடத் துணிந்தார்க்கே
sections.translit:
edhugaiyum mOnaiyum vENduvadhO emperumAn
thiruvaruL ninaindhu thudhipAdath thuNindhArkkE
sections.en: Does anyone who contemplates the grace and compassion of the Lord, and decides to sing His glory, truly need rhymes and alliterations in music?

sections.label: Anupallavi
sections.ta:
பாதம் பட்ட இடமெல்லாம் சாபம் நலியும்
திரு உறங்கும் பெரு நகரினிலோ வளம் மலியும்
sections.translit:
pAdham patta idamellAm sAbam naliyum
thiru uRangum peru nagarinilO vaLam maliyum
sections.en: All curses will be annihilated wherever the Lord’s feet touch. Prosperity will overflow in the city where Goddess Lakshmi resides.

sections.label: Charanam
sections.ta:
காலணியும் அரசாளும் கார்முகிலும் ஒரு திரண்டு
பாரெல்லாம் தழைத்திடவே கரைந்து நிற்கும்
செம்மண் வயலெல்லாம் செழித்து ஓங்கும்
சீர்மிகு சான்றோரும் மறை முறையே நடந்திடுவார்
sections.translit:
kAlaNiyum arasALum kArmugilum oru thiraNdu
pArellAm thazhaitthidavE karaindhu niRkum
semmaN vayalellAm sezhitthu Ongum
sIrmigu sAndROrum maRai muRaiyE nadandhiduvAr
sections.en: Even a mere pair of sandals will rule such a blessed land. Dark clouds will gather and dissolve to bring abundant rainfall, making the earth fertile. The farmlands will yield rich harvests, and the nation will flourish. Noble elders and learned scholars will live guided by the righteous path prescribed in the scriptures, without deviating from orthodoxy.

notes:
The anupallavi of the song is based on the episode of Ahalya’s sapa vimochanam (release from her curse). This event occurred when Lord Rama’s feet touched the uninhabited hermitage of Sage Gautama. Ahalya, his wife, had once been deceived by Lord Indra and thus incurred Sage Gautama’s wrath. He cursed her to become an inanimate stone, devoid of contact with any living being. Before departing, however, Sage Gautama granted her the boon that she would regain her original form when Lord Rama’s feet touched the hermitage. He also blessed her, saying she could reunite with him after worshipping Lord Rama. For details, see:
ஶ்ரீமத் வால்மீகி ராமாயண ஸாரம், உரை ஆசிரியர் அண்ணா, ஶ்ரீ ராமகிருஷ்ணமடம், மயிலாப்பூர், சென்னை 4, இரண்டாம் பதிப்பு, அஹல்யா சாப விமோசனம், பக்கம் 82-90.
The phrase “kalaniyum arasalum” in the charaṇam refers to an episode from the Ramayana, where Bharata placed Lord Rama’s sandals on the throne and ruled the kingdom as Rama’s representative until His return from exile. It is universally believed that any place where Goddess Lakshmi resides is blessed with boundless prosperity. The author further suggests that the presence of both Rama and Sita together in any place brings an even greater abundance of prosperity.
